mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past three months signals an active monetary easing cycle, reducing discount rates on future corporate earnings and increasing the present value of equities, leading to positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in less than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines over 3 months, or the average return is not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 9.0% over two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate revenue expectations, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in fewer than 60% of triggered instances, or the average return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in housing starts below 540,000 units over two consecutive months signals weakening consumer confidence and reduced residential investment, which depresses aggregate demand and leads to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in less than 60% of triggered instances, or the average return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production and a rise in the unemployment rate indicate a contraction in manufacturing output and labor market stress, signaling an imminent economic slowdown that reduces corporate profitability and drives negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in less than 60% of interaction-triggered instances, or the joint signal fails to outperform a simple average of individual series (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the CPIAUCSL above 217.5 over two consecutive months signals accelerating inflation, prompting the Fed to delay rate cuts or initiate tightening, which increases real discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in fewer than 60% of triggered instances, or the average return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) above 360,000 million dollars, combined with rising housing starts, indicates strong aggregate demand, boosting corporate revenues and investor confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in less than 60% of interaction-triggered instances, or the joint signal does not outperform individual series (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in non-farm payroll growth above 200,000 jobs per month, combined with a declining unemployment rate, signals a tightening labor market that may lead to wage pressures and inflation, prompting the Fed to raise rates, which reduces equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward 5-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in fewer than 60% of triggered instances, or the joint signal fails to outperform individual series (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth below 1.0% annualized, as measured by GDPC1, signals a weakening economy, reducing corporate earnings expectations and investor sentiment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in less than 60% of instances when GDPC1 growth is below 1.0%, or the average return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).
